newsitem.title: USA: Apple to announce layoffs on March 14.
newsitem.headline: Apple to announce layoffs on March 14.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc on March 14 expects to announce further details of its restructuring, including the number of layoffs that are planned, the company said on Tuesday.
In a letter to employees, Apple Chairman Gilbert Amelio said the troubled computer maker would also announce how much money it planned to set aside to pay for the program.

"On March 14, we are planning to give more detail on what we'll do, what we won't do, the number of layoffs and the charge we will take to second-quarter earnings" to cover the cost of the restructuring, Amelio said in the letter.

Last month, Apple, which has struggled in the face of sliding sales and an exodus of managers, unveiled a plan to consolidate its marketing and development units in an effort to cut costs and concentrate on key computer markets.
At that time, specifics of the plan, such as layoffs and possible charges, were not disclosed.
According to industry experts, Apple is expected to cut between 2,000 and 5,000 jobs from its worldwide workforce of 11,000 employees.
The company is also expected to take a charge of between $300 million to $350 million to pay for the cuts.
Previously, Apple said it planned to take a charge of about $323 million in the second quarter ending in June to pay for the acquisition of NeXT Software Inc.
The restructuring charge, coupled with the charge for NeXT, would translate into a substantial loss for Apple and would mark the second quarter in a row that the company had fallen in the red.
In the first quarter of fiscal 1997, Apple reported a loss of $120 million, reflecting weaker sales of its flagship Macintosh line.

Last month, Apple said it expected net sales in the second quarter of fiscal 1997 to fall short of the $2.13 billion reported in the first quarter. The company also said quarterly sales were expected to remain below the comparable year-ago periods for the remainder of fiscal 1997 and perhaps longer.
Apple, based in Cupertino, Calif., also said it did not expect to return to profitability until at least the fourth quarter of fiscal 1997, if not longer.
On Tuesday, Apple closed at 16-1/2, up 3/8.
